title: Papertrail sessionization & inference gotchas — field diary
content:
Meeting snapshot: 2024-11-01 call with Papertrail (integration kickoff). Attendees: Sam H. (Papertrail PM), Alex M. (client eng), Sasha P. (Redwood SE), Priya R. (solutions eng), Marco L. (infra). Quick high-level: customer runs conversational help widget embedded in mobile apps and web. They need sticky user sessions for context, low tail latency, and predictable cost for large daily MAU (~90k daily active sessions peak).

Main ask / constraints:
- Must support per-session KV cache so short conversations reuse prefixes (goal: reduce token generation cost by ~30%).
- Client cannot persist long-lived cookies (privacy regulations), so session keys are ephemeral (30–60s) and come from their auth service.
- Some clients are intermittent (edge devices with flaky connectivity) and will re-open sessions often; need idempotent replay protection to avoid duplicated tokens or double counting.
- P95 latency target <= 350ms for 95% of requests in hosted mode; fallback to smaller model on degradation.
- Expected average request seq len ~220 tokens; tail up to 1024 for multi-turn transcripts.
- Throughput: bursty patterns, up to 140 req/s regionally during promotions.
- Data residency: EU customers require Private deployment (VPC) for EU tenants; Papertrail prefers Redwood Dedicated for their US fleet.

Initial infra/serving implications (notes to self):
- KV cache TTL needs to align to their ephemeral session TTL. Current default prefix cache (15m) is too long — must implement short-lived session buckets or explicit cache-key lifecycle ops.
- If client issues new ephemeral session token on reconnect, they will get a fresh cache key -> cold start, increased cost. Consider mapping ephemeral token -> stable session id on Redwood side with short mapping table (redis) and GC. Privacy check: they said no PII mapping allowed; need to ensure mapping is opaque and encrypted, and optionally stored in customer-managed KMS in Private.
- Batching: their traffic is bursty but with many short requests; continuous batching may help but could increase latency. Need workload-aware batching config: aggressive batching only when observed queueing latency < 25ms.
- Model variants: route short/low-context queries to a smaller 6B variant; longer contexts to 13B+ with KV enabled. Must support automatic fallback policy if dedicated pool saturated.
- Token accounting: duplicated replayed requests inflate billing. Recommend idempotency-key header and dedupe window (server-side).

Gotchas surfaced on call:
- Mobile SDK sometimes loses in-memory session state during backgrounding; they re-auth and get fresh ephemeral token -> broken conversational continuity. Suggest: SDK emits persistent client-generated ephemeral session envelope (signed, rotates weekly) so we can map to same cache bucket without storing PII.
- Region failovers: client chooses closest region, but some customers travel cross-region and will hit different cache clusters -> context loss. Option: sticky routing by user home-region plus cross-region cache replication (expensive). Tradeoff doc needed.
- Edge-device clock skew causing out-of-order timestamps -> dedupe logic must be tolerant (use vector clock-ish monotonic counters from client).
- Privacy/legal: Papertrail's compliance forbids longer-than-necessary retention. If we do mapping table for ephemeral->stable id, need retention policy <= 24 hours by default and option for zero retention.

Immediate action items (owners + rough tickets):
1) Prototype ephemeral-token -> opaque-session mapping in Private flows; explore encrypted mapping with customer KMS. Owner: Marco L. Ticket: JIRA-ENG-2147. ETA: 2024-11-15.
2) Add optional idempotency-key header and server-side 5 minute dedupe window in hosted API (config flag per-customer). Owner: Priya R. Ticket: JIRA-SOL-339. ETA: 2024-11-09 (P0 for pilot).
3) Batching policy doc: define queue-latency thresholds and backoff strategy for Papertrail workload. Owner: Sasha P. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/papertrail-integration/pull/58. ETA: 2024-11-08.
4) Cost analysis: model-routing savings with KV cache reuse vs mapping-latency cost. Need numbers for 30/60/90s cache mapping TTL. Owner: Finance contact (cc: Evan T.). Ticket: FIN-468. ETA: 2024-11-12.
5) SDK recommendation: add persistent signed envelope to SDK to maintain session continuity across backgrounding. Owner: Alex M. (Papertrail) but Redwood to provide sample code + security review. Action: drop sample by 2024-11-05.

Design alternatives (brainstorm):
- Server-side sticky mapping: store ephemeral_token_hash -> session_bucket in Redis with TTL 24/48h. Pros: simple, fast. Cons: retention, customer compliance.
- Client-signed session envelope (preferred): avoids server-side PII; server only verifies envelope signature and uses envelope.id (opaque) as cache key. Requires SDK update.
- Token stitching at proxy: stitch short-lived tokens into longer-lived cache id using a HMAC of (device id + rotating secret) — privacy concerns.

Open questions for legal/privacy:
- Can Papertrail accept an opaque mapping that contains no user-identifying info but is deterministically tied to device fingerprint? (They worried about fingerprinting). Next step: have legal call w/ their privacy counsel.
- Minimum retention period allowed by EU customers for Private deployment mapping tables? (They likely want 0–24h).

Notes to self / cliff-notes for handoff to eng:
- Prioritize idempotency + dedupe: prevents billing surprises and repeated side effects in their downstream systems.
- Keep default cache TTL conservative (30s) for pilot; measure cache hit rate, cost delta; iterate.
- Provide per-route observability: session-level hit/miss rates, per-session token consumption, and P95 latency. Must be added to Console (per-customer dashboard).
- If we flip on cross-region cache replication, model capacity must be re-evaluated (more memory for KV). Explore sparse/sharded replication only for top 5% of active sessions.

Meeting follow-ups scheduled:
- 2024-11-05: SDK sample delivery + security review (Alex + Redwood SDK team).
- 2024-11-08: Internal batching policy doc + demo (Sasha).
- 2024-11-12: Cost sheet + finance review (Evan).
- 2024-11-15: POC for opaque mapping in Private (Marco).

Random quick notes / heuristics learned from other customers that may apply:
- Short-lived session buckets work best when client can provide any stable non-PII token (e.g., app-instance-id). If not, server mapping is the fallback.
- Aggressive continuous batching reduces token cost but often increases p95 unless you bound batching window tightly.
- Provide default fallback model route (smaller) and transparent cost delta shown in dashboard so customers can opt in.

Draft email blurb to Papertrail (for approval):
"High-level summary from today's call: we recommend adding an SDK-signed session envelope (small client change) to maintain cache continuity without storing PII. Short-term we will launch an idempotency header and a conservative 30s server-side mapping for the pilot to avoid billing duplication. Next week we will provide a cost projection comparing mapping vs no-mapping at 30/60/90s TTLs. Please confirm privacy/legal appetite for a 24h max mapping TTL for EU tenants so we can size Private accordingly."

-- end of scratch diary --

(Notes intentionally informal — migrate to confluence page once initial POC completes)
